identifier: Rulings the person (kyuhwan) made on 2026-09-21 about the standing of the pixel-size calibration cal-pixel-size-20260919, in answer to a direct question about what ends its twelve rows before their stated fifteen years.
grade_rule: E5, via the `assumed:` prefix, exactly as src_person_ruling_20260919 argued it. A ruling is not a reading (operator_read, E3), not a recollection (operator_recall, E5) and not a calibration event (E2). It takes E5 because what stands behind it is the person's judgement rather than an observation, and the grade says so whether the judgement is good or bad.
what_was_asked_and_what_came_back: Asked which of four candidates the store implies would end the twelve pixel-size rows -- a recalibration, an objective change, a camera change, or a change in the optics between objective and camera. Two came back: there will be no recalibration and the present values stand, and a change of objective means reading a different row rather than losing one. The other two were not addressed.
one_of_the_two_is_an_intent_and_the_stor: WITHDRAWN AS AN ENTRY ON 2026-09-21, THE SAME DAY IT WAS FILED, AND THE DECISION LIVES HERE INSTEAD. The no-recalibration half was filed as the entry `pixel_size_calibration_is_not_repeated` at E5 under this source, with a note saying the fit was a seam. The seam was not a seam, it was an error: `plan.md:1259 @6d587b3` settles it outright -- "A policy takes no grade -- because it is a decision, not a claim. P2's four parts attach to A CLAIM ABOUT THE WORLD." A decision not to recalibrate is not a claim about the world, so it takes no grade; and kb_entry.schema.json REQUIRES `grade`, so there is no way to file it in kb/entries/ without giving it the one thing it must not have. The removal is forced by the schema, not chosen. THE RIGHT READING WAS AVAILABLE AND THIS SEAT ARGUED PAST IT: librarian_agent/CLAUDE.md says 'we do not exceed Y is policy, belongs to a person, and is not knowledge', and the seat read that as scoped to safety because the sentence sits beside envelope/safety.*. The safety ceiling is the INSTANCE; the principle is general. manager-simulation caught it from the other side, having hit the same distinction the same day in check 72's `within_tolerance`.
note: Kept separate from src_person_ruling_20260919 for the same reason that record was kept separate from the recall of its own day: a source record is per occasion, and folding two days' rulings into one would make the date on an entry stop saying when the person said it.
what_survives_and_where: The decision itself, here: the person ruled on 2026-09-21 that cal-pixel-size-20260919 will not be repeated and the twelve values it produced are the ones in use. That is recorded and findable by anyone reading this source or src_operator_calibration_20260919, which carries the same ruling under `standing_2026_09_21`. What it is NOT is a graded claim, and it is not reachable through kb_query -- which is correct, because kb_query answers questions about the world and this answers a question about what we intend. The ruling's other half IS a claim about the world and stays an entry: objective_change_selects_a_pixel_size_row.
